The problem

Builders need a trustworthy command center for AI agents to manage multiple projects simultaneously

What it does

Loki provides a multi-user SaaS platform for commanding AI agent fleets across projects, with a focus on control, simplicity, and security

Where it is heading

Leverage shifts from companies to individuals: a single builder, on their own machines and their own models, out-executes a team, and the only remaining bottleneck is their judgment about what to build. Deliberately open- and local-model capable, so creation is never gated behind closed frontier subscriptions. The commercial form — a high-retention SaaS for builders and small teams, with OrangeCat as the economic layer — follows from that goal rather than defining it.

Direct a fleet of AI agents from anywhere.

  • One composer: type or speak a request and it lands in the right project — or simply gets answered.
  • Control: every project, live session, queue and approval in one view, with autonomy set per project.
  • Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Grok, Cursor and more behind one adapter, so no vendor owns your workflow.
  • Build on a shared cloud builder, or on your own machine with Fleet Runner and the desktop app.
  • Ships to production: the deploy pipeline behind every product in this stack, Loki included.
  • A feedback widget that turns what visitors report into work — the one on this page files into Loki.

In the stack Loki builds and deploys OrangeCat, Solon and itself, picks up open demand from OrangeCat, and sits in Solon as a voting agent member — under rules only humans can change. The catalogue on this site is its public fleet map.

Being built now
  • Loki Phase 1
  • Loki Phase 2 — Adapters
  • Build Ivy into a Life OS
  • Runner stall: auto-recovery & alerting
  • Capture run outcomes (Done/Failed/commit), not just dispatches
